t: What does ha!shh do?
a: It holds incoming notifications based on your rules and delivers them in batches at your chosen hours. The notification text is never read to decide whether to hold it; only the source app and arrival time are used. Notification content is read and displayed solely on your phone by default; the app has no internet permission, and no data ever leaves your device.

t: How do I complete the initial setup?
a: When you first open the app, the Initial Setup Wizard starts. You review the privacy information, grant notification access and battery permissions, then pick a lifestyle profile that fits you (Student, Office Worker, Night Shift, Freelance / Flexible). Setup also configures the nighttime Sleep schedule upon first launch, so the app is ready to use immediately once setup is complete. If you exit the wizard midway, you can resume it from the card on the Today screen or via Settings → Tools → Initial Setup Wizard.

t: Which permissions are required?
a: Two essential permissions are needed: notification access (required to hold and batch-deliver notifications) and battery/background permission (to ensure scheduled delivery times aren't delayed). You can view both under Settings → Device permissions, where each displays either "Permission granted" or "Permission required".

t: What is on the Today screen?
a: In the center is a 24-hour day dial: 12 at the top, 18 on the right, 00 at the bottom, and 06 on the left. The app icons of pending notifications appear on the dial, with nearby times spaced out to prevent overlap. Below it, you'll find the Pending card deck, the next delivery time, the archive card, and the Time Saved summary (which also estimates battery savings from prevented screen wake-ups).

t: How do I view pending notifications?
a: On the Today screen, tap the Read all › link on the Pending card. You can also tap Deliver all now to receive all held notifications right away. Tapping a notification opens the app it came from. In the card deck, swipe a card right to mark it as read, or swipe left to snooze it for 30 minutes. If you want to undo your action, simply tap the Undo button that appears at the bottom of the screen for 4 seconds.

t: Can I read notification content in the app?
a: Yes. Showing notification content is enabled by default; content is read and displayed safely only on your device. If you prefer not to see it, you can toggle it off under Settings → Content and calm → Show notification content. When disabled, only the app name, time, and hold reason are displayed.

t: How is Time Saved calculated?
a: By default, 1 minute is counted as saved for each notification held without interrupting you. You can adjust this duration between 0.5 and 5 minutes under Settings → Content and calm → Time per interruption. To disable the summary, turn off the Time saved summary switch in the same section. The card also displays estimated battery savings gained by preventing unnecessary screen wake-ups.

t: How do I set up a rule for an app?
a: In the Rules tab, tap the app. Four options will appear: Immediate, Hold, At delivery time, Block. The behavior you choose will apply to all notifications from that app.
q: how to make a rule for an app

t: I want an app to never be held
a: In Rules, tap the app, choose Immediate, and tap the Never hold (deliver in every mode) option that appears below. This ensures notifications from that app arrive immediately no matter which mode is active. For safety, Android system and SIM notifications (network, carrier, system alerts), as well as emergency calls and alarms, are never held under any circumstances.
q: never delay notifications for an app
make an app bypass all modes

t: I only want to see messages in apps like Instagram (type filter)
a: In Rules, tap the app and open the Type Filter panel with Select type ›. Presets are available: Messages only, Likes only, Likes + comments, Reset. For each type, you can individually choose Default, Immediate, At delivery, or Block. Filtering is based strictly on the app's notification channel/type; content is never read.
q: only get direct messages on instagram

t: Can I manage apps as a group?
a: Yes. On the Rules screen, tap New Group to bundle multiple apps into a single group and manage them with one rule. A group can contain up to 100 apps.

t: Where are the apps I permanently blocked?
a: Go to Settings → Tools → Blocked. Here you can see your blocked apps along with a log of notifications received from them (app and timestamp); you can unblock any app by tapping Unblock.

t: What are the modes?
a: There are four built-in modes: Normal, Focus, Sleep, and Sports. The hold duration and behavior of each mode are configured separately. When a mode expires, notifications held during that mode are delivered all together at the end of the mode rather than at scattered times. You can edit any mode via Adjust › on its card under Your Modes in the Schedule tab, or add your own mode with + Custom mode.

t: How long does a manually selected mode last?
a: When you manually activate one of the quick modes, it stays active until you turn it off; scheduled transitions will not override your selection. When you are ready to return to your schedule, simply tap the Return to schedule button.
q: how long does manual mode stay on

t: How do I set up the weekly schedule?
a: In the Schedule tab, you will see the days of the week and hour blocks. Tap a day and drag the block handles to adjust the times. Use the + Mode, + Custom for today, and + Delivery time buttons to add new blocks or delivery times.

t: Adding a mode interval from the dial
a: Tap the + button next to the dial on the Today screen. Select an interval on the dial (e.g., 18:00–24:00 Focus, 00:00–06:00 Sleep); hours advance in 15-minute increments. A warning will appear if an interval overlaps. You can edit or delete added intervals later.

t: How do I change delivery times?
a: In the Schedule tab, tap the Edit delivery times & Daily rhythm › link in the Adjust › panel on the mode card. Pending notifications will be delivered in their original state at the next scheduled batch delivery time.

t: I work shifts
a: You'll find Shift schedule under Schedule tools. Enter your cycle and shift hours once; ha!shh automatically calculates which shift you are on each day. When enabled, "Shift schedule · today …" is displayed in Schedule.
q: how to set up rotating shifts

t: How do I view past and future days?
a: You can navigate between months using Month view under Schedule tools. You can view stats for past days and set up custom schedules for future dates.

t: Sports mode and spoiler shield
a: Under Schedule, tapping Adjust › on the Sports card opens Sports Settings. Notifications from your chosen sports apps are held until the match ends; other apps arrive normally. If Enable spoiler mode is on, your chosen shield apps are also held until the match ends. You can also add keywords (e.g., goal, score); this matching only runs when content permission is enabled and happens strictly on your phone.

t: What is the Archive, and where is it?
a: It keeps notifications you want to save—such as coupons, bills, and spending—in organized folders. Open it from the 📦 Archive button at the top of the History tab or from the archive card on the Today screen. Archive data is stored strictly on this phone and in encrypted form.

t: How do I add a notification to the archive?
a: While reading pending notifications or in History, tap the Archive › link next to a notification and select a folder. You can create your own folder using ➕ Create New Folder... Any archive records you add or edit manually are permanently preserved and never automatically deleted.

t: Automatic archiving (archive rules and groups)
a: Auto-archive is enabled by default. It automatically saves only important notifications into relevant folders: bank payments, coupons, completed purchases, and bills/due date reminders. Prices shown in ads are not archived. Manually added or edited entries are always kept. Amounts are displayed in your phone's local currency. You can disable auto-archive or select which types to include under Settings → Privacy and data → Auto-archive. In the Archive screen, tap ⚙ Rules to add custom rules based on app, sender, or keyword.

t: Coupon wallet
a: When you switch to the Coupons folder in the Archive, the Coupon & Promo Wallet appears at the top. Active discount codes and campaign coupons are collected here, and you receive a reminder as their expiration date approaches.

t: Browsing by app and searching in the Archive
a: In the Archive, tap the 📱 By app button to select a specific app and view only its records. Use the search bar to search by app name or notification content.

t: Exporting the Archive and uploading to Drive
a: In the Archive, tapping Export Archive presents three options: 🔒 Encrypted Archive (.hashh) (password-protected and the recommended secure format), Unencrypted JSON (.json), and Unencrypted CSV (.csv · Excel / Spreadsheet). You can save the resulting file anywhere you choose, such as Google Drive or local storage, via Android's share menu. Because ha!shh has no internet permission, it never uploads files to any server itself.
q: export notifications to csv or json

t: Fingerprint lock
a: Go to Settings → Privacy and data → Fingerprint lock. Three options are available: Off, Archive and notification content only, and Entire app (on every launch). The lock can be opened with your fingerprint, face recognition, or phone PIN/password.

t: How long notification history is kept
a: During setup, ha!shh asks how long you want to keep notification history: delete after 7, 30, 90, or 365 days, or Don't auto-delete, I'll clean manually. The recommended option is 30 days. You can change this later under Settings → Content and calm → Notification history retention period. If you haven't set a duration, no records are ever deleted automatically. If history starts taking up too much space, a "Clean up old records?" card appears on the Today screen. You can clean records older than 30 days if you wish; the number of records to be deleted is shown beforehand and requires your confirmation. If you choose "Not now", it won't ask again for 14 days. Archived records are never affected by this cleanup. Displaying notification content (title and body) in history requires Show notification content to be on; content is stored strictly on this phone and encrypted.

t: Screenshot blocking
a: Settings → Privacy and data → Block screenshots on sensitive screens is an optional security setting that is turned off by default. When enabled, it prevents taking screenshots in the vault, lock screen, and panels showing notification content, and hides content in the recent apps preview.

t: Home screen widgets
a: You can add ha!shh to your home screen as a widget. Four sizes are available (2x2, 4x1, 4x2, 4x3). The widget displays the next delivery time, the active mode, the pending notification count, and the apps with the most pending notifications. Larger sizes (4x2 and 4x3) include a list of pending notifications and a one-tap "Mark all as read" button. It adapts to your selected theme; tapping the clock displays the current time.
q: see pending notifications on home screen

t: What is a quiet alert?
a: It is a single silent, non-vibrating summary line in your phone's notification bar for held notifications: it shows who sent notifications, how many there are, and the next delivery time. You can choose Off, Selected apps…, or All pending notifications under Settings → Content and calm → Quiet alert. If app icons in notifications are enabled, expanding the summary line reveals the icons of pending apps.

t: Live notifications like deliveries
a: If you accidentally dismiss notifications with progress tracking, such as package deliveries, food orders, or music players, you'll see them in History with a "⚡ Live" badge. Tapping the row immediately opens the corresponding app.

t: Quick settings tile
a: You can add a ha!shh tile to your phone's top notification pull-down via Settings → Tools → Quick settings tile. The tile shows the pending count and the delivery time; you can configure what tapping it does from the same menu.

t: Mode by Wi-Fi
a: The Settings → Tools → Mode by Wi-Fi option provides step-by-step instructions on automatically switching modes when connecting to home or work Wi-Fi using your phone's routines app (such as Samsung Modes and Routines). Location permission is not required.
q: auto switch mode at home or work

t: Changing themes
a: Under Settings → Appearance, you'll find Paper, Light, Dark, and System themes, along with Night (Petroleum Velvet) and Day (Cream Paper). You can also switch themes easily using the Sun/Moon button on the Today screen. You can choose to have the home screen icon match the theme's color whenever the theme changes.

t: App language
a: Under Settings → Appearance → App language, you can choose directly from 10 languages (and the system language) inside the app without having to open your phone's system settings.

t: App icon
a: Under Settings → Appearance → App icon, you can set the home screen app icon color to match your theme. On some phones, changing the icon may remove it from the home screen and place it back in the app drawer; simply drag it back to your home screen.
q: app icon disappeared from home screen

t: Minimal view
a: When Settings → Content and calm → Minimal view is enabled, the Today screen displays only the dial, a single mode button, and the pending list; the Rules and Schedule tabs are hidden. Your configured rules continue working in the background as usual.

t: Simple UI on low battery
a: If Settings → Appearance → Simple UI on low battery is enabled, ha!shh automatically switches to minimal view and pauses animations when your phone enters battery saver mode to reduce power consumption.

t: Desk view on landscape rotation
a: When Settings → Appearance → Desk view on landscape is enabled, rotating your phone sideways turns the screen into a desk clock featuring a large clock, active mode, week strip, next delivery, and pending notifications. You can choose which sections to display and use your own photo as a frame or background. The screen can stay awake while charging, and its low-power layout conserves battery.

t: Notification Report and Statistics
a: Under Settings → Tools → Notification Report, you can review your notification rhythm, daily and monthly distribution, focus/sleep balance, and time saved along with estimated battery savings from prevented interruptions all on a single screen. There is no separate "Statistics" item; all usage stats are consolidated into the Notification Report. You can also share the report as an image if you like.

t: How do I invite a friend?
a: Go to Settings → Invite and earn rewards. You'll see your code under Your Invite Code; tap Invite to share via any messaging app, or tap Copy Code.

t: How does my invite count increase?
a: Your friend installs the app and enters your code in the I Have an Invite Code field. They then send you the thank-you code generated on their phone (Send Thank-You Code). You enter that code into the Enter Thank-You Code field and tap Add. The same person cannot be counted twice.

t: What are the rewards?
a: You earn the First invite badge at 1 invite, Paper wallpaper at 3, Silent circle badge at 5, Night wallpaper at 7, and ha!shh ambassador badge at 10. Your invited friend also receives the "Joined via invite" badge. Unlocked wallpapers become available as backgrounds for the Today screen under Settings → Appearance → Flow Wallpaper; you can also save them as PNGs via Save wallpaper as image.

t: How do I back up my rules?
a: Go to Settings → Backup → Export to file. Your rules, modes, and weekly schedule will be saved to a file on your phone. There is no cloud/internet backup, and notification contents are never included in this file.

t: How do I restore from a backup?
a: Go to Settings → Backup → Import from file and select your backup file. The app displays the file's contents; Merge adds new rules while keeping your existing ones, while Replace replaces all rules with those in the backup.

t: Sharing a rule template
a: You can share your rules with a friend via Settings → Backup → Share rule template. Notification contents are strictly never shared.

t: Sending feedback
a: Settings → Send feedback opens your email app with a pre-formatted template. Your notification content and custom rules are not attached; you can review and edit the email text before sending.

t: Promo code
a: Under Settings → Tools → Redeem promo code, you can activate a Google Play promo code directly through the Play Store.

t: Notifications are not held and arrive immediately
a: The most common reason is that notification access was turned off. If the Settings → Device permissions → Manage notification access row says "Permission required", tap it and enable ha!shh. Also check if Immediate or Never hold is selected for that app; tap the app in the Rules tab to verify. For safety, phone calls, alarms, and Android system and SIM notifications (network and carrier alerts) are never held in any mode.
q: why are notifications coming through immediately

t: Notifications did not arrive at the delivery time
a: Most often, your phone's battery saver has stopped ha!shh in the background. Tap the Settings → Device permissions → Battery and background row; use the Turn Off Battery Optimization button and, if your device brand is recognized, the Open Device-Specific Settings button. The System health row shows connection status; if it says "Disconnected", tap Reconnect there. When a mode's duration ends, notifications held during that mode are delivered all together at the end of the mode, not at staggered intervals.

t: Deliveries are delayed on Samsung
a: In your phone settings, go to Battery → Background usage limits and add ha!shh to the Never sleeping apps list. If it's in the Sleeping apps list, remove it from there. The Open Device-Specific Settings button in ha!shh takes you straight to the Samsung battery screen.

t: Deliveries are delayed on Xiaomi, Redmi, or POCO
a: In your phone settings, go to Apps → ha!shh, turn on Autostart, and set Battery saver to No restrictions. Locking ha!shh in the recent apps screen also helps. The Open Device-Specific Settings button in ha!shh opens the corresponding Xiaomi screen.
q: redmi notifications not delivering on time

t: Deliveries are delayed on Huawei or Honor
a: In your phone settings, go to Battery → App launch, turn off automatic management for ha!shh, and enable Auto-launch, Secondary launch, and Run in background. The Open Device-Specific Settings button in ha!shh attempts to open this screen.

t: Deliveries are delayed on Oppo, Realme, OnePlus, or Vivo
a: In your phone settings, enable Auto-launch and Allow background activity for ha!shh, and disable battery optimization. The Open Device-Specific Settings button in ha!shh attempts to open the relevant screen for your brand.

t: I restarted my phone, what happened to pending notifications?
a: ha!shh automatically checks and restores pending records after a restart. If any notification could not be restored, a "Check delayed notifications" prompt will appear; when that happens, simply open the respective apps to check them.

t: Did my manually selected mode change on its own?
a: A manually chosen mode remains active until you turn it off; scheduled changes do not override it. To return to the schedule, tap the Return to schedule button.
q: schedule not starting after manual mode

t: An app doesn't appear in the list
a: Try typing the app's name into the search box. If the app is not installed on your phone or hasn't sent any notifications yet, it might not be listed; check back after its first notification arrives. The app might also be inside a category: tap a category in Rules to see its apps.
q: why is app not showing up

t: No notification types show up in the type filter
a: Types are learned dynamically as the app sends you notifications of that type. Wait until you receive a few notifications from the app, then check again under Rules → app → Select type ›. Categorization is based on the app's notification channels; content is never read.
q: how does type filter detect categories

t: I permanently blocked an app and want to undo it
a: Go to Settings → Tools → Blocked, switch to the Blocked Apps tab, and tap Unblock.

t: Fingerprint lock option doesn't appear or work
a: A screen lock (fingerprint, PIN, or pattern) must be enabled on your phone, and Android 9 or higher is required. After enabling a screen lock in your phone settings, try again via Settings → Privacy and data → Fingerprint lock.

t: Notification content is not showing
a: Showing content is enabled by default. If it is not showing, verify that Settings → Content and calm → Show notification content is turned on. If you want to read notification contents in the History tab later on, check your Notification history retention period setting: records older than your chosen duration are deleted; if no period was selected, nothing is ever deleted automatically.
q: body text not showing in history

t: Screenshots of the History screen turn out black
a: This is not a bug; it is an optional privacy setting. If Settings → Privacy and data → Block screenshots on sensitive screens is enabled, taking screenshots is blocked in the vault, fingerprint lock, and content-viewing screens. This setting is off by default; if you want to capture screenshots, simply disable this option.

t: Why doesn't ha!shh request internet permission?
a: The app was intentionally built without internet permission. Your notifications, rules, and archive never leave your phone for any server. If you want to transfer a file out (like a backup or archive), you do so yourself via the system share menu.
q: does ha!shh send data to servers

t: Where is the Archive?
a: You can tap the 📦 Archive button at the top of the History tab or open it from the archive card on the Today screen. Auto-archive is enabled by default; it automatically saves only bank payments, coupons, completed expenses, and bills/due date reminders to their respective folders. Ad prices are never archived. Records you add or edit manually are never deleted and always remain.

t: I want to save my archive to Google Drive
a: In the Archive, tap Export Archive and choose a format; 🔒 Encrypted Archive (.hashh) is the most secure. In the share menu that appears, select Drive. The archive is never uploaded to backups or the cloud automatically; it only exports to a file when you choose to do so.

t: I can't add an app to a new archive folder
a: In the Archive, you can add or remove apps from a folder using ⚙ Manage Apps.

t: No coupons are showing up in the archive
a: Coupons are gathered from notifications archived into the Coupons folder. Add a notification to Coupons using Archive ›, or set up an auto-archive rule for your store apps under ⚙ Rules → + Add Rule.
q: how to add coupon to archive

t: I accidentally dismissed an order notification
a: You can find that notification in the History tab marked with a "⚡ Live" badge. Tapping the row opens the app containing the order so you can view its latest status.

t: Tapping a notification returns to the home screen
a: Tapping notifications in the pending list and History opens the app they came from. Returning to the home screen when tapping on the dial panel is a known issue currently being resolved.
q: tapping notification goes to home screen
app doesn't open when tapping notification

t: I accidentally acted on a pending card (marked read or snoozed)
a: When you swipe a card left or right in the pending card deck on the Today screen, an Undo bar appears at the bottom of the screen for 4 seconds. Tap it to immediately reverse the action.
q: how to undo mark as read

t: Where can I change the app language?
a: There is no need to visit your phone's system settings. You can instantly switch ha!shh to your preferred language (10 languages supported) under Settings → Appearance → App language.

t: Desk view doesn't open
a: To have desk view open when rotating your phone sideways, make sure Settings → Appearance → Desk view on landscape is enabled. You can also manage options like keeping the screen on while charging and the low-battery layout from the same screen.
q: phone rotated desk view won't open

t: How do I add a home screen widget?
a: Long-press an empty space on your phone's home screen and select ha!shh from the widgets menu. You can choose from four different sizes (2x2, 4x1, 4x2, 4x3) to suit your needs.
q: how to add widget to home screen

t: Where can I find statistics and the notification report?
a: There is no separate "Statistics" menu; all usage statistics and distribution charts are combined into Settings → Tools → Notification Report. Here you can see daily and monthly notification counts, focus balance, time saved, and battery savings.

t: I changed the app icon and it disappeared from the home screen
a: On some phones (e.g., Samsung), changing the icon removes it from the home screen and returns it to the app drawer. Simply drag ha!shh from your app drawer back to the home screen.
q: app icon vanished after changing theme

t: I can't find the quick settings tile
a: Swipe down twice from the top of your screen to open the notification panel. If the tile isn't visible, swipe right to check subsequent pages. If it's missing, add it again via Settings → Tools → Quick settings tile.
q: missing ha!shh tile in status bar
how to add notification panel tile

t: Invite code not accepted
a: You can enter the code with or without hyphens; capitalization does not matter. You cannot enter your own code, and an invite code can only be used once. If the code is still rejected, a character may be mistyped; ha!shh detects single-character typos, so ask your friend to copy and resend the code.

t: Thank-you code says "This code does not belong to you or is invalid"
a: A thank-you code is generated specifically for the code of the person who invited you; someone else's thank-you code cannot be added to your count. Ask your friend to resend the code using Resend My Thank-You Code. If it says "This invite has already been counted", that person has already been credited to your count.
q: this code does not belong to you

t: How do I restore from a backup?
a: Go to Settings → Backup → Import from file and select your backup file. Merge keeps and updates your current rules, while Replace overwrites everything with the backup file. The app warns you if the file is corrupted or too large (over 512 KB).

t: I'm switching phones, what happens to my settings?
a: On your old phone, create a backup via Settings → Backup → Export to file and transfer the file to your new phone (e.g., via Drive or a cable). Install ha!shh on the new phone and load it via Import from file. To transfer your archive as well, use Export Archive → 🔒 Encrypted Archive (.hashh) on your old phone. You will need to regrant notification access and battery permissions on the new phone.

t: I want to delete all my data
a: Go to Settings → Privacy and data → Delete all local data. Rules, history, pending records, and preferences will be permanently wiped; this action cannot be undone. If you wish to back up first, use Export my data in the same section. Archive records are also permanently erased by this action.

t: I want to report an issue
a: Settings → Send feedback opens your email app with a pre-written message. Your notification content and custom rules are not attached.
